items.title: Nvidia is cheap on paper, so why won't the market buy it?
items.summary: Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia giving back about half of its Jensen Huang rally and why a stock growing sales 60% to 70% can trade at 10 times earnings, whether the Alice Wong affair was a "hit job," and what next week's Senate testimony means for the stock.

items.title: Lucid Group (LCID) Starts Driverless Robotaxi Testing, Is It A Bargain?
items.summary: Lucid Group (LCID) just moved its Gravity robotaxi program into fully driverless testing with Nuro and Uber in the San Francisco Bay Area, marking a concrete step toward commercial autonomous ride hailing. Lucid Group’s latest robotaxi milestone comes after a rough stretch for investors, with the 1-year total shareholder return down about 80% and the 5-year total shareholder return down close to 99%. items.title: Lucid (LCID) Stock Still Trades At A Premium Following A 99% Slide
items.summary: Lucid Group has seen its stock slide sharply in recent years, even as the company pushes ahead with new vehicle programs and partnerships. That mix of falling share price and evolving business plans raises a basic question for investors who focus on Lucid Group: how much are you really paying today for its sales? items.title: Lucid Group (LCID) Begins Fully Driverless Robotaxi Testing On Bay Area Roads
items.summary: Lucid Group (NasdaqGS:LCID) has started fully driverless testing of its Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area. The pilot is being run in partnership with Uber and Nuro, with testing focused on commercial ride hailing and goods delivery use cases. Management has confirmed fleet commitments from partners as part of this robotaxi program, indicating a defined deployment pathway beyond the trial phase. items.title: Motional retools for the robotaxi race
items.summary: Once a pioneer in autonomous driving, Motional is reasserting itself in the robotaxi race with a new AI-driven approach and the manufacturing muscle that comes with being majority-owned by a global automaker.

items.title: Bernstein’s $250 Target Says DoorDash’s Selloff Went Too Far
items.summary: Key TakeawaysDoorDash stock is 31% below its August high after Amazon gave Prime members free Uber Eats delivery and the Justice Department reportedly moved to review DoorDash’s Instacart deal. Bernstein cut its DoorDash target to $250 from $270 and kept its Outperform rating, a target 53% above the stock.
